summary: Theofil Simenschy worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Alexandru Ioan Cuza University (1910–1913, PhD ~1923–1927), where he also served as Assistant (1926), Docent (1938), and Professor of Classical Languages and Comparative IE Philology (1942–1968).

Theophil Gubler was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Basel (~1897–1903) under Jacob Wackernagel and worked as a teacher at Gymnasium am Münsterplatz from 1906 to 1934.

Theos Bernard specialized in Tibetology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned an L.L.B. from the University of Arizona (~1927–1931), followed by an M.A. (~1934–1936) and a Ph.D. (~1936–1943) under Herbert Schneider at Columbia University.
Thibaut d'Hubert is an Indologist who held a post at the University of Chicago and served as a Vertretungsprofessor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Thich Nhat Hanh worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Báo Quốc Temple, University of Saigon, Princeton, and Columbia. His academic posts included positions at Princeton, Columbia, Vạn Hạnh University, and Cornell.
Thich Thien Nghiem is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Delhi (attested 2012) under the supervision of Shalini Singhal.

Thierry Mathou is a scholar in Tibetology. He studied at EDHEC Business School (~1982–1985) and Sciences Po (~1985–1987), and has served as an Associated Political Scientist at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique.

Thierry Meynard works in sinology and philosophy. He earned a PhD in philosophy at Peking University under Yulie Lou (~1999–2003), became Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University (~2006), and directed The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies (2012).

Thinh Canh Quang is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of the West (attested 2007) supervised by Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya, after studying under Lewis Lancaster and Ananda Guruge.

Thinlay Ram Shashni is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He has held positions at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, serving as editor (attested 1997, 2007) and Associate Professor, IN-charge/HoD (attested 2026).

Thinley Dorji Bhutia worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a Tibetan Teacher and Boarding Superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School, Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1994), and Chief Editor of Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1994).

Thinley Norbu Rinpoche was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who studied at Mindrolling Monastery and under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (Dudjom Rinpoche), later teaching students including Albion Moonlight Butters, Chönyi Drolma, and Garab Dorje Rinpoche.

Thomas A. Forsthoefel works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Georgetown (B.A.), Loyola University Chicago (M.A.), and University of Chicago Divinity School (Ph.D. under Paul J. Griffiths), later serving at Mercyhurst University (attested 2007).

Thomas A. Tweed is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a PhD at Stanford University (~1984–1989) and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1993–2008).

Thomas Alexander Wise was an Indologist and historian who earned an M.D. from the University of Edinburgh (~1821–1824). He served in the Indian Medical Service (1827–1851) and was Principal of Hooghly Mohsin College (1834).

Thomas Andrew Lumisden Strange was an Indology scholar. He was educated at Westminster School (~1770–1774) and studied at the University of Oxford, where he earned a B.A. (~1774–1778) and a D.C.L. (~1818).

Thomas Athol Joyce worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Dulwich College and Hertford College, Oxford (~1897–1902, M.A.), and served as Deputy Keeper at the British Museum from 1902 to 1938.

Thomas B. Ellis specializes in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania and served as Assistant Professor of Religion at Appalachian State University (attested 2009).
Thomas Best Jervis was an Indology and history scholar. He held posts with the East India Company (~1813–1841), the Survey of India (~1819–1841), and the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

Thomas Blom Hansen works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Aalborg University (2013–2018) and held posts at the Universities of Natal, Edinburgh, and Amsterdam, Yale University, and Stanford University (appointed Professor of Anthropology in 2010).
